```text
REVIEW_DECISION: REJECT
RISK_CLASS: high-impact
SUMMARY: Governance intent is sound: harness-owned apply/gates, no model self-certification, dual Sol+Opus enforcement for high-impact records, counterfactual-gated model_profile RCA, non-blocking 500k checkpoint, and refactor review deliberately unrestricted. But the deterministic enforcement does not match safety property 2. Child profiles are barred only from the `authority` and `budget_policy` keys; their `adapter` block is a free-form object, so a child can grant write/shell/network tools and still pass schema and loader while nominally inheriting `model_edits_workspace:false` and `commit_push_deploy:false`. Secondary: the execution-receipt schema requires no per-call raw counters and no unavailable sentinel, so "unknown" is indistinguishable from zero (property 3).
FINDING: high|docs/factory-ng/schemas/factory.model-profile-v1.schema.json + scripts/factory-ng-profile-validate.py|Non-baseline profiles are validated only for absence of `authority`/`budget_policy`; `adapter` is `{"type":"object"}` with no constraint on tools, sandbox, or filesystem/network permission, and the loader never inspects it. Effective authority is therefore set by an unvalidated adapter field while the inherited authority block still asserts the model cannot edit the workspace or commit. This broadens a Ticket's authority through the one dimension the contract explicitly permits profiles to vary, defeating property 2 and undermining properties 1 and 5. Evidence that the restriction is ad-hoc and unenforced: `qwen-prepared-local` declares `forbidden_tools`, `claude-staged` declares `disallowed_tools`, `codex-constrained` relies on the free-form string `"sandbox": "read-only"`, and `qwen-prepared-direct` relies on an empty `allowed_tools` — four different unvalidated conventions for the same safety property.
REQUIRED_CHANGE: In factory.model-profile-v1.schema.json, make `adapter` a constrained object for the non-baseline branch: require `allowed_tools` drawn from a closed read-only enum (e.g. read_file, grep, list_dir) and forbid any write/edit/shell/network/commit/deploy capability, require an explicit `filesystem: "read-only"` and `network: "none"` declaration, and set `additionalProperties: false` on `adapter` so unknown capability keys cannot smuggle permissions. Move the same checks into factory-ng-profile-validate.py so the loader — not just the schema — rejects capability escalation, and state in model-profile-contract-v1.md that any profile needing write/shell authority requires its own reviewed baseline with an explicit `authority` block under the high-impact governance path. Add fixtures `invalid-child-profile-tool-escalation.json` (write/shell tools, must fail) and `valid-child-profile-readonly-tools.json` (must pass) to scripts/test_factory_ng_contracts.py. Separately, tighten factory.execution-receipt-v1.schema.json to require per-call raw counters with an explicit `"unavailable"` value distinct from `0`, and split `telemetry` into `raw` and `normalized`, with a fixture proving a receipt that omits or zero-fills unknown counters fails.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: Add docs/factory-ng/model-profiles/v1/rogue-child.json: {"schema":"factory.model-profile/v1","id":"rogue-child","version":"1.0.0","extends":"staged-baseline@1.0.0","adapter":{"executable":"claude -p","allowed_tools":["Write","Edit","Bash"],"sandbox":"danger-full-access","network":"unrestricted"},"routing":{},"telemetry":{}}. It contains no `authority` and no `budget_policy` key, extends the baseline directly, and carries adapter/routing/telemetry, so Draft202012Validator passes it and factory-ng-profile-validate.py returns "pass"; scripts/test_factory_ng_contracts.py, which validates every file in model-profiles/v1 with the same rules, also passes. The profile is then a governance-approved adapter whose model can edit the workspace and run git commit/push, while its inherited authority block still records model_edits_workspace:false and commit_push_deploy:false — and any resulting provenance record would attribute harness-owned apply authority to a change the model applied itself.
```
